2609.02111.title: Disease Burden over Skin Tone: Decomposing the Dermatology-AI Generalization Gap
2609.02111.paper_summary: Dermatology artificial intelligence (AI) models are predominantly trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections, yet they are increasingly proposed for deployment in resource-constrained settings where patients differ from training populations along two confounded axes: skin tone and disease distribution. We investigate whether poor generalization is primarily caused by skin-tone underrepresentation or disease-distribution shift. We evaluate a cancer-trained baseline (ResNet-50 fine-tuned on HAM10000 and ISIC 2019), two dermatology foundation models (DermLIP and MONET), and a general-purpose vision model (DINOv3) as frozen feature extractors. Models are evaluated on a tone-stratified disease-matched dataset (Diverse Dermatology Images, DDI) and a disease-shifted tone-diverse dataset (Skin Condition Image Network, SCIN). Our results show that disease-distribution shift contributes more than skin tone in the evaluated settings. The cancer baseline decreases from 0.62 to 0.21 balanced accuracy when transferred to unfamiliar clinical conditions, while the within-disease skin-tone gap is smaller (0.10-0.18) and inconsistent. Label-free representation analysis shows that this failure reflects a representational limitation rather than only missing output labels: cancer-specialized features poorly cluster unfamiliar conditions (kNN purity lift +0.06 over chance), whereas dermatology-pretrained features retain stronger transferable structure (+0.23). Finally, we show that representation quality predicts recoverable performance under lightweight adaptation. Starting from dermatology foundation models, approximately ten labeled examples per clinical category recover most attainable performance. We release the evaluation protocol and code to support reproducible auditing of dermatology AI generalization.
2609.02111.paper_summary_zh: 皮膚科人工智慧（AI）模型主要是在以淺膚色和癌症為焦點的影像資料集上訓練的，然而它們越來越多地被提議用於資源有限的環境中，在這些環境中，患者與訓練人群在兩個混淆的軸上存在差異：膚色和疾病分布。我們調查了較差的泛化是否主要是由於膚色的代表性不足或疾病分布的變化所致。我們評估了一個以癌症為訓練基準的模型（在HAM10000和ISIC 2019上微調的ResNet-50）、兩個皮膚科基礎模型（DermLIP和MONET），以及一個通用視覺模型（DINOv3）作為凍結的特徵提取器。這些模型在一個按膚色分層的疾病匹配數據集（多樣化皮膚科影像，DDI）和一個疾病轉變的膚色多樣化數據集（皮膚狀況影像網絡，SCIN）上進行評估。我們的結果顯示，在評估的環境中，疾病分布的變化對模型的影響大於膚色的影響。當轉移到不熟悉的臨床條件時，癌症基準的平衡準確率從0.62下降到0.21，而同一疾病內的膚色差距較小（0.10-0.18）且不一致。無標籤表示分析顯示，這一失敗反映了一種表徵限制，而不僅僅是缺少輸出標籤：專注於癌症的特徵在不熟悉的條件下聚類效果較差（kNN純度提升+0.06），而皮膚科預訓練的特徵則保留了更強的可轉移結構（+0.23）。最後，我們顯示表示質量預測在輕量適應下可恢復的性能。從皮膚科基礎模型開始，每個臨床類別大約需要十個標記示例即可恢復大部分可達的性能。我們發布了評估協議和代碼，以支持皮膚科AI泛化的可重複審計。
